To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have proposed a novel framework to transform the design problems of sparse CSEs and TIRs into the problem of finding sparsest-approximations of a vector in a given sparsifying dictionary.

we propose a design and analysis framework for channel shortening equalizers that is based on the sparsest-approximations of a vector in a sparsifying dictionary, that we compare several choices for the sparsifying dictionary under this framework, and that we evaluate the worst-case coherence for these dictionaries, which is a measure of their sparsifying ability.
the sparseness of the channel response can be exploited to improve the performance of channel shortening equalizers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of sparse FIR CSEs for broadband communications.
the design of sparse FIR channel shorteners and the associated sparse TIR filters.
the problem of designing sparse FIR filters with the objective of channel shortening.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the case of sparse CSE, the proposed framework is able to design a sparse CSE that outperforms the existing state-of-the-art sparse CSE designs.
the proposed framework is a very promising approach for the design of the sparse CSE and sparse TIR FIR filters.
the proposed framework is very useful for the design of CSE and T IR filters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the design of sparse FIR CSE and T IR filters under a given coherence constraint is a problem of sparsest approximation of a given vector under the sparsifying dictionary that has the lowest coherence.
we provide a unified design and analysis framework for the design and performance evaluation of sparse FIR CSE and T IR filters.
we have provided the design and analysis framework for the sparse CSE and sparse TIR filters and have also compared several sparsifying dictionaries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sparsity of the CSE and TIREs can be exploited to reduce their complexity, and that the choice of the dictionary is crucial to the effectiveness of the sparsest-approximations.
the choice of a dictionary for sparse CSE and/or TIR filters is a crucial design parameter that determines the performance and complexity of the overall channel shortening system.
the proposed framework can be applied to a variety of problems in signal processing and communications where the objective is to design a sparse FIR filter.
